LACSON CLARIFIES PHOTO WITH THE DISCAYAS

Senate President Pro Tempore Ping Lacson, chairman of the blue ribbon committee investigating anomalous flood control projects, says the photo showing him with controversial contractors Curlee and Sarah Discaya was taken in April, when their son — then a party-list nominee — visited his Taguig office to invite him to a rally in Davao.

Lacson said the Discaya couple later joined the meeting, which lasted 15–20 minutes, but he declined their invitation out of respect for his friend, Senate President Tito Sotto, whose nephew, Pasig Mayor Vico Sotto, was running against Sarah Discaya.

“I did not know the Discayas and that was the first and only time outside of the Blue Ribbon committee hearings that I met them... I hope this clarifies whatever insinuations are being attached to this said photograph,” Lacson said.

The photo was posted by Rep. Kiko Barzaga, with the caption: “CTTO, please investigate the validity of this image of Senator Lacson’s private meeting with the Discaya.” | @eimorpsantos

🚨🇵🇭 MAGNITUDE 6.9 EARTHQUAKE KILLS 20+ IN PHILIPPINES

A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck Cebu province in the central Philippines just before 10 p.m. local time Tuesday, killing at least 20 people and injuring 37 others.

Four buildings collapsed, including a sports complex where four victims were playing basketball. 

The dead included a Bureau of Fire Protection member, three Philippine Coast Guard members, and a child trapped in rubble.

Cebu Governor Pam Baricuatro ordered immediate delivery of relief supplies and deployed equipment to clear roads. 

Six bridges and one road are impassable.

Schools and government buildings will remain closed Wednesday.

Cebu province is home to 3.2 million people. 

The Philippines sits on the Pacific "Ring of Fire" where tectonic plates meet.

Source: New York Times
